newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli, Palestinian negotiators meet on Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israeli, Palestinian negotiators meet on Hebron.

text.p: Israeli negotiators proposed adjustments to a long-delayed Israeli troop withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron in formal talks with the Palestinians on Monday, Israeli security sources said.

Palestinians however denied Israel had proposed any modifications to the Hebron plan during a closed meeting of the joint Israeli-PLO steering committee at Erez crossing between Israel and the Gaza Strip.

The Israeli sources said Israel had proposed its forces retain control of hilltops overlooking heavily armed enclaves housing some 400 Jewish settlers in the heart of the city of 100,000 Arabs, when parts of the city are turned over to Palestinian police.

The sources said Israel also suggested limits on weapons allowed to Palestinian police, and the creation of buffer zones dividing Israeli troops from PLO forces in Hebron, the only West Bank town with Jews living in it and a flashpoint of violence.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said recent violence in which 59 Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed made ensuring security for 400 Jewish settlers in Hebron even But a senior PLO official denied Israel had proposed changes in the Hebron plan at Monday's talks, and reiterated the Palestinian opposition to altering the Hebron deal agreed to by Israel's previous government, ousted by Netanyahu in May.

"No proposals were submitted by the Israelis today. We discussed the general framework of the Hebron agreement," the official told Reuters. "The Palestinians insisted on their position that no modifications or changes in the agreement would be accepted," he said.
Talks between the sides are to resume on Tuesday at 1400 GMT at Erez.
The PLO official said the sides were wrangling over the venue of future non-stop talks.
"Both sides are studying where the next talks will take place next week. The Palestinians have asked for negotiations in Egypt. The Israelis want them to take place in Israel," he said.
